_about: Free play ('open history'). The war starts as it did on 1 September 1939 and after that no computer-run nation follows history's plan: each one's staff weighs up its fronts every month and decides for itself. 'temper' is national character: attackAt is the strength ratio (our attack against their defence near the front, forts, terrain and season counted) at which a staff opens an offensive, persist the ratio below which it calls one off, minOdds the odds a single attack needs. A nation with no attackAt never opens an offensive of its own, though it still defends and counter-attacks. 'mood' is how far a nation's nerve differs from one war to the next (each war draws its own, by seed). The staff's habits: an offensive that gains no ground for 'stall' months is called off unless the odds are still good, and the army then rests 'rest' months before it tries again. A front that can only be attacked head-on into fortifications counts 'headOn' times as strong. An offensive under way keeps up to 'commit' times the enemy's strength for itself, so that a second one is not opened with the same troops. A front is a serious one when the enemy's strength on it is at least 'major' of this nation's whole army. Each month's attacks are bounded: the main thrust goes along the easiest road to the nearest enemy capital, 'thrust' regions deep ([opening month of a nation that makes war by speed, any other month]) with the ground on either side, and elsewhere only prizes, bulges in the line and places held by no more than 'weak' divisions are attacked. The road starts only where the army has at least 'foothold' of the force it has at its strongest point. At a ratio of 'general' or more the whole of the enemy's front is pressed. A side-show is taken on to a depth of 'bound' regions, a theatre overseas 'boundOverseas'. With the enemy within 'guardWithin' regions of the capital, 'guard' corps are kept in it. 'ops' are the great decisions history took, written as choices: a staff may take one up when its conditions hold (the 'if' list reads as in diplomacy.json, plus 'quiet' for no serious land front, 'collapsing:FRA,0.07' and 'month:5,6,7'), the months of the war lie between 'from' and 'to', the odds in prospect are at least 'ratio', and the month's draw comes in under 'chance'. It then spends 'prep' months bringing the army up before it declares war on the 'declare' list, and attacks for at least 'push' months. 'season' lists the months of the year, numbered from 1 for January, in which it may begin. A 'side' operation needs no build-up and does not take the main army: a landing, or a small neighbour. 'join' moves a neutral onto that side of the alignment track when it marches. 'staging' is a force kept ready for the operation until it is launched, and 'landings' name the corps that go by sea and the shores each one tries in turn.

impatience._about: A war nobody is fighting makes bolder generals. 'after' is months without a land battle between a nation and the enemies on a front (or since their war began): past the first term a staff opens an offensive at 'ratio'[0] of the strength ratio it would usually wait for, past the second at 'ratio'[1], but never below 'floor'. A nation with no attackAt of its own opens one past the last term if the ratio reaches 'any'. A main effort opened this way runs for 'effort' months before anyone asks what it has gained, and for those months single attacks go in at 'odds' (shorter than the nation's minOdds). A staff that stays on the defensive still makes local attacks once the first term has gone by: up to 'locals' a month, each at odds of 'local'[0] or better (past the second term, 'local'[1]), and it keeps at them while the last one is no more than 'effort' months old.

descent._about: The second front. A nation with sea lift that has been at war with an enemy for 'after' months with no land battle against him and no troops in touch with ground he holds keeps 'force' corps by a quay and crosses the sea: to a harbour of his that is unguarded, or guarded at 'odds' or better, with a crossing no riskier than 'risk' and no more than 'near' times its own strength within a march of the beach. It tries in a month with chance 'chance', and waits 'every' months after a landing. The hardest level has rules of its own for the player's coasts (difficulty.json).
